name: Kashmir’s Sufi Shrines and Sacred Streets
difficulty: Walking and steps vary by site · discuss before booking
season: Dates by request · worship, local access and conditions apply
route: Srinagar · Khanqah-e-Moula · Jamia Masjid · Hazratbal · Makhdoom Sahib · Charar-e-Sharief
description: A five-day private Muslim shrine journey with a Srinagar base and a dedicated day for Charar-e-Sharief.
highlights: Four nights at one Srinagar base

itinerary.title: Welcome to your Srinagar base
itinerary.description: Transfer to the agreed stay and allow time to settle in. Discuss the purpose of your visit, walking comfort, dietary preferences and any observance you hope to attend. The coordinator checks visiting arrangements before the sightseeing days; a late arrival is kept free of compulsory stops.
experiences: Arrival transfer at the agreed time
A planning conversation about interests and appropriate visiting etiquette
itinerary.routeNote: Current custodian permission, worship arrangements, weather and individual walking suitability decide access and the final sequence. No ceremony or religious interior is guaranteed.

itinerary.title: Shah-e-Hamdan and the old-city lanes
itinerary.description: Give the old city a focused day around Khanqah-e-Moula and Jamia Masjid. The guide chooses a workable lane route, with a short vehicle link if useful. Dastgeer Sahib at Khanyar can be requested if access and the group’s pace allow; otherwise it replaces another visit. Keep prayer times free and do not assume access to a particular interior or ritual.
places: Dastgeer Sahib, Khanyar: an optional substitution
experiences: A guided introduction to the local shrine tradition
An optional quiet market or kahwa pause
itinerary.routeNote: Current custodian permission, worship arrangements, weather and individual walking suitability decide access and the final sequence. No ceremony or religious interior is guaranteed.
itinerary.meals: Breakfast and dinner proposed; other food separately agreed

itinerary.title: Lakeside devotion and the Hari Parbat slopes
itinerary.description: Choose a measured visit to Hazratbal and Makhdoom Sahib, allowing breaks between them. Makhdoom Sahib involves an approach that must be discussed around steps and walking comfort. The guide confirms permitted visitor areas and adjusts the programme around worship. Guests preferring a gentler day can choose just one site and more time at the lake.
places: Makhdoom Sahib: approach and access to confirm
experiences: A quieter lakeside pause when the route permits
itinerary.routeNote: Current custodian permission, worship arrangements, weather and individual walking suitability decide access and the final sequence. No ceremony or religious interior is guaranteed.
itinerary.meals: Breakfast and dinner proposed; other food separately agreed

itinerary.title: A separate day for Charar-e-Sharief
itinerary.description: Travel to Charar-e-Sharief for a dedicated visit associated with Sheikh Noor-ud-Din Noorani, also known as Nund Rishi. Allow time for the town and the visit without adding distant shrines on the same day. A short Yusmarg extension is an alternative only when the road, weather and daylight allow and the party wants it; it is not an automatic inclusion.
places: Optional Yusmarg-side outing only if separately agreed
experiences: Time for the shrine visit at a locally suitable hour
A meal break before the return road stage

itinerary.title: Leave time for the onward journey
itinerary.description: Have breakfast if departure timing permits, then take the agreed transfer. Airport and road buffers come before any extra visit. An early flight may require leaving before breakfast service; confirm this and any packed food with the stay. Additional shrines or outlying sites need a revised itinerary rather than a last-minute detour.

extensions.description: Request a separate southern-valley extension for Aishmuqam’s Zain-ud-Din Wali shrine and an agreed Pahalgam-area base. Confirm the shrine approach, steps, local access and return transfer rather than adding it to the Charar-e-Sharief day.
